date.note: A16: CMS announced the measurement on 17 September 2024, before the arXiv preprint (2024-12-18) or the Nature publication (2026); the announcement date is used per A16.

key_value.quote: a precise measurement of the W mass, of 80 360.2 ± 9.9 MeV

name: High-precision measurement of the W boson mass
notes: The CMS news page is titled "CMS delivers the best-precision measurement of the W boson mass at the LHC"; the plain summary attributes that wording to the collaboration.

significance.note: A measurement, not a discovery; no significance is quoted.
significance.quote: we reach a precise measurement of the W mass, of 80 360.2 ± 9.9 MeV, in agreement with the standard model prediction.

summary.plain: CMS measured the mass of the W boson, which the collaboration calls the best-precision measurement of the W mass at the LHC, and found it in agreement with the Standard Model prediction. The paper notes that a measurement by the CDF collaboration at the Tevatron disagrees strongly with both the Standard Model expectation and the other measurements.
summary.technical: W → μ ν events from 2016 13 TeV data, high-granularity maximum likelihood fit to muon kinematics with in situ constraints on theory inputs: m_W = 80 360.2 ± 9.9 MeV.

title: High-precision measurement of the W boson mass with the CMS experiment
why_it_matters: The abstract says the W and Z boson masses are uniquely related in the Standard Model and that a precise determination of their masses is important because quantum loops of heavy, undiscovered particles could modify this relationship.
